title: Lemon and Caper Chicken
subtitle: Italian pan-fried chicken breast with a quick lemon and caper butter sauce
excerpt: Butterflied chicken breast pan-fried until golden, finished in a quick sauce of butter, lemon, and capers. Ready in 25 minutes and elegant enough for a dinner party.
sourceNotes: Piccata is an Italian-American cooking method in which thin escalopes of meat are coated lightly in flour, pan-fried, and finished in a lemon and caper pan sauce. It is widely popular across Italian-American restaurants.

content.text: Butterfly the chicken so each breast is no more than 1cm thick; this ensures it cooks through quickly without drying out.

items.prepNote: zest of one, juice of both

content.text: Season the chicken well. Dust lightly in flour on both sides; shake off the excess.
Heat the olive oil and half the butter in the frying pan over a medium-high heat.
Fry the chicken in two batches for 3 minutes per side until golden and cooked through. Set aside on a warm plate.
Lower the heat. Add the garlic and cook for 1 minute.
Add the capers and lemon zest. Cook for 30 seconds.
Pour in the stock and lemon juice. Let it bubble for 2 minutes, scraping up any bits from the base of the pan.
Remove from the heat. Whisk in the remaining butter in small pieces until the sauce is glossy.
Stir in the parsley. Return the chicken to the pan, spoon the sauce over, and serve immediately.

items.symptom: Sauce has split and looks greasy.
items.cause: Butter was added over too high a heat.
items.fix: Remove from heat completely before whisking in the cold butter.

items.cause: Overcooked or breast was too thick.
items.fix: Butterfly thinner next time; 3 minutes per side is enough for 1cm.

items.cause: Too much lemon juice or not enough butter to balance.
items.fix: Swirl in an extra knob of butter off the heat.
